headline: VIRIDIAN METALS EXTENDS KRAKEN MAIN 1.5KM IN STEP-OUT — 15m at 1.1% CuEq Confirms Wide Copper System in Newfoundland
snippet: Viridian Metals (CSE: VRDN) announced today that step-out drilling at Kraken Main in Newfoundland and Labrador has returned 15 metres of 1.1% copper equivalent, extending the system 1.5 kilometres beyond the initial drill footprint. New assays confirm higher grades and substantially greater mineralized thicknesses than the original Exploration Target, building the case for a resource estimate on what is shaping up as a district-scale copper discovery at a time when copper's structural supply deficit is driving premium valuations for in-jurisdiction North American copper projects.

headline: BANNERMAN'S ETANGO URANIUM MINE ENTERS FULL-SCALE CONSTRUCTION AFTER FID — Namibia Project Moves to Build Phase as Term Prices Hit Records
snippet: Bannerman Energy has made its final investment decision on the Etango uranium project in Namibia and entered full-scale construction, becoming one of the very few new primary uranium projects worldwide to reach the build phase in this cycle. The FID arrives as long-term uranium contract prices hit nominal records above $96 per pound — validating the economics of projects that were marginal at $50/lb uranium just two years ago and marking Namibia, alongside Kazakhstan and Canada, as a top-tier uranium development jurisdiction for the decade ahead.

headline: GOLD SLIDES TO LOWEST SINCE AUGUST AT $4,032 — Pre-FOMC Rate Fear Deepens; Silver Steadies at $54 After Testing $53 Floor
snippet: Spot gold slipped to approximately $4,032–$4,050 per ounce on October 23, its weakest level since early August 2026, as markets priced in the probability of a Federal Reserve hold but continued to de-risk ahead of the October 27–28 FOMC meeting. Silver recovered slightly to around $54 per ounce after testing the $53 floor earlier this week — still down more than 50% from January's $121 record. The gold-silver ratio remains near 73, historically elevated, and a re-compression once the FOMC catalyst clears could be sharp for silver-leveraged junior producers.

headline: AZINCOURT ENERGY PUTS FIRST HOLES INTO LABRADOR'S SNEGAMOOK URANIUM — Radioactive Zones Hit as Long-Term Price Hits Nominal Record
snippet: Azincourt Energy (TSXV) has put drills into its Snegamook project in Labrador for the first time, with initial holes intersecting zones of elevated radioactivity that confirm the presence of the uranium mineralizing system targeted by the exploration model. The timing is notable: the release coincided with reports that the long-term uranium contract price has hit its highest level in nominal terms — a milestone that suggests utilities are locking in supply at structurally elevated prices, creating a more durable demand signal for exploration-stage uranium projects in Tier-1 Canadian jurisdictions.

headline: COPPER, URANIUM AND LITHIUM SUPPORT LEVELS ALL AT RISK — Pre-FOMC Selloff Tests Key Technical Floors Across the Critical Metals Complex
snippet: FXEmpire's October 23 multi-commodity technical analysis identifies simultaneous support tests in copper, uranium, and lithium — three metals where junior mining valuations are most sensitive to price breaks — ahead of the FOMC meeting. The analysis argues that the selloff has pushed all three to levels where a close below support would trigger further institutional selling, while a bounce on a Fed-pause confirmation could create sharp snapback moves for junior producers and developers across all three metal categories.

headline: USA RARE EARTH DOWN 74% FROM ITS ALL-TIME HIGH — Motley Fool: Reshoring Story Intact, But Pre-Revenue Reality Demands Patience
snippet: A Motley Fool analysis published October 22 asks whether USA Rare Earth (NASDAQ: USAR) — down approximately 74% from its lifetime high and 15% year-to-date — represents a generational reshoring opportunity or a cautionary tale about investing in pre-revenue critical minerals plays. The piece highlights that excluding the recently acquired Serra Verde rare earth operation in Brazil, USA Rare Earth is still fundamentally pre-revenue, and the departure of CEO Barbara Humpton effective October 1 adds leadership transition risk at a critical juncture for a company whose entire thesis depends on government procurement support and consistent execution on its Round Top project in Texas.

headline: NVRO METALS RAISES C$35M TO ACQUIRE NORTHERN TERRITORIES RESOURCES — Placement Closing ~Oct 27 as Junior Consolidation Wave Continues
snippet: NVRO Metals is raising up to approximately C$35 million through a private placement expected to close around October 27 to fund its acquisition of Northern Territories Resources, consolidating a package of mining claims in the Northern Territory of Australia. The deal is part of a broader pattern of junior consolidation accelerating across the TSX-V and ASX as elevated gold and copper prices make it economically rational to aggregate fragmented exploration tenements into development-scale asset packages — a trend that historically accelerates in the 12–18 months following a commodity price cycle peak.

headline: HOCHSCHILD MINING CONFIRMS 2026 GUIDANCE — Silver-Gold Mid-Tier Holds Outlook as Spot Prices Remain Well Above Operating Plan
snippet: Hochschild Mining confirmed its 2026 production and cost guidance in a recent operational update, noting that realized gold and silver prices remain substantially above the assumptions embedded in its annual operating plan. For investors tracking mid-tier silver producers, Hochschild's confirmation is a data point that the silver price — despite its sharp decline from January's $121 record to the current $54 range — is still generating robust operating margins at its Peruvian and Chilean operations, reinforcing the thesis that silver mining equities at current valuations may be underpricing the production economics at today's spot.

headline: GOLDMAN SACHS SEES 950,000-TONNE EX-US COPPER DEFICIT IN 2026 — Weekly Analysis Shows LME Stocks, BHP Labour Deal Masking Structural Gap
snippet: Copper's October 22 weekly brief documents a disconnect between short-term bearish price signals — LME inventory builds, copper falling to a five-week low near $14,089 per tonne, and BHP's tentative Chilean labour settlement removing a supply catalyst — and Goldman Sachs' revised structural demand model showing an ex-US supply deficit of 950,000 tonnes in 2026 narrowing to 220,000 tonnes in 2027. The gap between the headline inventory trend and Goldman's deficit forecast is the key unresolved tension for copper junior developers: spot price weakness compresses near-term project economics, but a 950kt deficit means the long-term thesis for new primary copper supply has never been stronger.

headline: BARRICK MINING AT 12X EARNINGS AND 2.2% YIELD WITH GOLD AT $4,000 — The Contrarian Case for the World's Second-Largest Gold Miner
snippet: A Motley Fool analysis from October 21 makes the contrarian case that Barrick Mining is materially undervalued at roughly $40 per share — trading at just under 12 times forward earnings and 11 times trailing earnings with a 2.2% dividend yield — even as JP Morgan simultaneously raised its price target to $55 with an Overweight rating. The piece argues that the market is underpricing Barrick's leverage to sustained $4,000-plus gold by applying a trough multiple to a business now generating structurally higher free cash flow, particularly across its Nevada and Pueblo Viejo operations, and that the rate-fear selloff in gold equities creates an entry point that may not last beyond the October 28 FOMC clearing event.
